evidence.field: oracle-bone graph formation and graphic development
evidence.text: The entry analyzes oracle-bone 生 as 屮 over 一, with 一 representing ground: a plant growing from the soil. It says early bronze forms retain this structure; a dot was later added below 屮 as a decorative stroke and became a horizontal stroke, making the lower part resemble 土. Small seal retains the sprout-emerging-from-ground idea. This is a modern paleographic analysis, not a claim that every early variant is visually identical.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—生

evidence.source: 許慎《說文解字》 as transcribed by CUHK
evidence.text: The entry quotes 說文:「生，進也。象艸木生出土上。」The historical account describes plants emerging above soil; CUHK interprets 進 (‘advance’) as an extended sense. Shuowen is a later lexicographic explanation and is not independent proof of the oracle-bone form’s details.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—生

evidence.text: The entry cites oracle-bone 生 in a prayer for childbirth (合集34078), 生月 in 合集8648正, and adjectivally for live/fresh birds (合集116正) and a live deer (合集10270). It reports 生月 as ‘following month’ and 生 in 多生 as 姓, while noting an alternative analysis 多甥. These cited examples establish reported usages, not a chronology among them; the 生月 interpretation remains disputed.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—生

evidence.text: The entry cites bronze 生 for childbirth in 叔尸鐘, occur/produce in 中山王方壺, a living creature in 中方鼎, lifespan in 蔡姞簋, and as a phonetic loan for 姓 on 兮甲盤. It also cites Warring States manuscripts for childbirth in 清華簡二《繫年》 and living opposed to dying in 上博竹書一《緇衣》 slip 19. The entry supplies no artifact date for each cited token, so none is assigned here; the examples do not order senses chronologically.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—生

evidence.text: The related 姓 entry says 生 supplies sound in 姓; oracle-bone 姓 has 女 plus 生, while bronze 姓 has 人 plus 生. It separately reports oracle-bone 生 used for 姓 in 多生, with 多甥 offered as an alternative. This concerns 生 as a whole graph borrowed/used for another word, distinct from 屮’s semantic role within 生. The pronunciation and reconstruction rows supplied locally show 生 and 姓 modern Mandarin shēng and xìng, and Baxter–Sagart MC sraeng/sjengH and OC *sreŋ (variant row-specific notation)/*seŋ-s; these comparisons alone do not establish the historical borrowing.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—生

gaps: Unicode official character-specific pages for 生 and 屮 both returned internal errors. The local exact 生 row is available, but no current reading for 屮 was supplied or independently verified. No sound-component role is proposed for either 屮 or 一 in 生.
The Baxter–Sagart upstream page was inaccessible. Exact local rows were preserved with their notation, but no external verification of those rows was possible.

Although CUHK describes 生’s graphic development from oracle bone through bronze to seal, no dated artifact chain is given for each shape. Its cited inscription examples are not assigned individual artifact dates here.

The ‘next month’ analysis of oracle-bone 生月 is disputed; alternatives include ‘this month’ or a different reading. Available evidence does not prove semantic chronology from sprouting/growth to the month use.

The evidence reports early childbirth, live/fresh, life, producing/occurring, lifespan, and 姓 loan uses independently. It does not establish a securely dated transition chain among all these meanings.
The dossier’s proposed conservative form 𤯓 and claims about its relation to 㞷 and 𡴀 were not independently investigated in this run; no corruption or ancestry conclusion is offered.

The Commons illustration pages were inspected for descriptions and rights, but their SVG pixels were not visually inspected. Captions identify them as modern vector depictions and do not claim visual verification of image contents.
The seal Commons description cites a secondary image source and a separate permissions provenance; no exact specimen date is supplied for the seal-style glyph.
No repeated-source bulk extract is recommended: reuse terms for complete dictionary text databases were not verified, and concise character-specific paraphrases suffice.
